clue.text: Action by head required for new title

definitions.note: a phrase describing a thing: the legal document needed to take a new name

parts.note: an action or act is a deed
a poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax levied per head

explanation.surface: A headmaster's decision is needed before someone can be given a new title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just sets DEED beside POLL. A deed poll is the British legal document a person signs to change their name officially.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone changing their name in Britain does it formally through this signed legal document, so it is what a new name needs.

clue.text: Failing to change sides

explanation.surface: Someone is losing their grip and switching allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a flaw or shortcoming; as a verb it means to desert one's country or party for another.

clue.text: Instruction which might result in one getting cautioned

indicators.note: the clue says the answer's letters could produce the word that follows once reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teaching that could land a pupil with a telling-off from the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: rearranging the answer 'might result in' CAUTIONED. Its nine letters reworked give the answer; 'which' and 'one getting' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is the giving of instruction, teaching in a structured way.

clue.text: Took firm action to speed things up

explanation.surface: Someone made a decisive move to hurry matters along.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to insist firmly; taken literally it is pressing the accelerator pedal of a car to go faster.

clue.text: A noted soporific

parts.note: noted means set to musical notes, so this is a sleep-inducing piece of music, a song sung to send a baby off

explanation.surface: A famous sleeping drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle song is sung to soothe a child to sleep, so it is soporific music.

clue.text: It follows a gale at sea, too

definitions.text: It follows a gale at sea

explanation.surface: Something that trails a storm on the ocean, also.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A SWELL, the first reading is the heavy rolling sea left behind by a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rolling wave follows a storm at sea; the phrase also means also or in addition.

clue.text: Opposing psychiatry, remains in good shape

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses therapy nonetheless stays fit.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shrink' is slang for a psychiatrist, so resisting one is opposing psychiatry; fabric labelled this way keeps its size in the wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally hostile to a therapist, called a shrink; as a fabric label it means cloth that will not get smaller when washed.

clue.text: Provide some point to a joke

parts.note: E is east, one point of the compass
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: Give a joke a bit of edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only links. 'point' suggests a punchline, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit out or supply someone with what they need is to provide for them.

clue.text: Dame Fortune's aristocratic sister?

parts.note: Dame Fortune personifies luck; a sister with a noble title would be called Lady rather than Dame

explanation.surface: A noblewoman related to the personification of fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck personified as a woman is another name for Fortune, given the noble title Lady.

clue.text: Meaty language

explanation.surface: Speech that is substantial and full of content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meaty' does not mean substantial here: it points to the cut of meat sold by butchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ox tongue is a meat eaten cold in slices; a tongue is also a language, as in mother tongue.

clue.text: Mistake by a serving man

parts.note: the serving man is a tennis player serving, not a servant, and his error is the call made when a serve lands out

explanation.surface: A blunder made by a waiter or butler.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, a serve that misses the service box is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an error generally, and in tennis it is the call for a bad serve.

clue.text: Peer about like Humpty Dumpty

explanation.surface: Gaze all around, in the manner of the nursery-rhyme egg.
explanation.walkthrough: Humpty Dumpty, an egg in an English nursery rhyme, would literally appear round.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer about is to glance in every direction; Humpty Dumpty, being egg-shaped, has a rounded appearance.

clue.text: Prisoners closely linked at work

parts.note: the convicts are not friends but literally shackled together by fetters while labouring outdoors

explanation.surface: Inmates who form close bonds while doing their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Convicts made to labour while chained to one another form such a group.

clue.text: Plane crash in the Himalayas

definitions.note: a description, not a noun: the definition says where the place lies, the mountain kingdom among those peaks

indicators.note: a crash wrecks the word so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aircraft comes down in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Mountain crashes are a real headline, so 'Plane crash' reads as one event; 'crash' is the anagram signal, and the definition is a location rather than a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies along the Himalayan range, home to Everest, so it is found among those mountains.

clue.text: Where the farmer will go to sow?

definitions.text: Where the farmer will go to sow?

parts.words: Where the farmer will go to sow?
parts.note: sow is not planting seed but a female pig, so the farmer visits her pen

explanation.surface: A field where the farmer plants his seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A female pig lives in a pen on the farm, so a farmer seeing to her goes there.

clue.text: Fickle boy about to betray one's trust

indicators.note: the boy's name goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
to rat on someone is to betray them

explanation.surface: An unreliable lad is about to let a friend down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', with 'to betray' following as a verb, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpredictable and changeable is inconsistent, as a fickle person is.

clue.text: Complete journey to meet train, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters may be arranged another way, signalling an anagram

parts.note: nine letters taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Finishing a trip by going to the station to meet a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only links. A train or bus that ends its run at a station is said to do this there.
explanation.definitionFit: A service that ends its route at a station stops there, finishing its run.

clue.text: The best player is a defender

explanation.surface: The top performer on the team plays at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A title winner is the top competitor, and someone who champions a cause stands up for and protects it.

clue.text: Gift for the poor employee on strike

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in a farmhand
workers who strike are said to be out

explanation.surface: Charity given to a worker who has walked off the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity in the form of money or food given free to people in need.

clue.text: But do they fit under slacks?

definitions.text: But do they fit under slacks?

parts.words: But do they fit under slacks?
parts.note: slacks are trousers, under which close-fitting legwear is worn, but the word also suggests loose, and these are the opposite of loose

explanation.surface: A question about whether underwear fits beneath casual trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-fitting nylon legwear covers the legs and waist, and could be worn beneath trousers.

clue.text: Cuban's leader's a star turn in company

indicators.note: the scrambled word sits inside the abbreviation
a turn here spins the word round so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Cuban politician is the star performer in a theatre troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star turn' reads as a headline act, but 'turn' is the anagram signal on the word star; 'a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Cuba for decades after its revolution, so he was the leader of Cubans.

clue.text: Officer cut off in pass

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
someone cut off is isolated or lone

explanation.surface: A military officer is stranded in a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army rank, above a major, is an officer.

clue.text: Uncertain opportunity

explanation.surface: An opening that may or may not come off.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means accidental or unplanned, as in a chance meeting; as a noun it is an opening or occasion to act.

clue.text: Damp is needed for "love-in-a mist"

indicators.note: the clue's own phrase love-in-a mist says the zero goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A garden flower name, love-in-a-mist, set beside a word for wetness.
explanation.walkthrough: Love-in-a-mist is a blue garden flower; read literally it puts love (O) in MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly wet, as a cloth or the air can be, is damp.

clue.text: Entrance to bay

explanation.surface: The way into a coastal cove.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an opening through which something enters, such as a valve, and also a small arm of the sea, a narrow bay.

clue.text: Poet, playwright and forger

explanation.surface: A man who wrote verse and drama and also faked documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Goldsmith was an Irish poet and dramatist; 'forger' is someone who forges, works, precious metal, not a counterfeiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith wrote poems and the play She Stoops to Conquer; a craftsman who works precious metal into jewellery shares the name.

clue.text: Descriptive of gains from false sickness benefit claim?

definitions.text: Descriptive of gains from false sickness benefit claim?

parts.words: Descriptive of gains from false sickness benefit claim?
parts.note: money obtained dishonestly, and here literally obtained by claiming to be poorly

explanation.surface: A phrase for money made by faking illness to claim welfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Money acquired dishonestly is described this way, and here the dishonesty is pretending to be unwell to receive it.

clue.text: Once more makes a profit

explanation.surface: Someone turns a profit yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A GAIN, the second reading is a profit made.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means a second time; read as two words it is a profit, what a successful trader makes.

clue.text: Observing what comes from a dumb-bell?

definitions.text: Observing what comes from a dumb-bell?

parts.words: Observing what comes from a dumb-bell?
parts.note: a dumb bell is a mute bell, so it makes no ringing sound, while observing means remarking or noticing

explanation.surface: Watching what a gym weight produces.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO TING: a bell that is dumb gives no ding. A dumb-bell is really a gym weight, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To be remarking on or taking note of something is to be observing it.

clue.text: Everybody present and of sound mind

explanation.surface: Every person attending is perfectly sane.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the words mean every person is in attendance; as an idiom someone mentally sharp and sane is described so.
